Gross profit was 258.7 million baht, increased by 59.5 million baht, representing an increase of 29.9%, mainly due to
revenue growth from sales and services following ongoing branch expansion and revenue recognition from newly
opened branches.
Gross profit margin in Q1’26 was 46.1%, decreased from 48.0% in Q1’25, mainly due to higher food raw material costs
and promotional campaigns implemented to maintain customer traffic and same-store sales amid cautious consumer
spending conditions.
In addition, some newly opened branches remained in the early stage of operations, resulting in less favorable cost
efficiency during the early ramp-up period. The Company continues to closely manage gross profit margins through menu
mix optimization, food cost control, and operational efficiency improvements to to support margin discipline and
sustainable profitability over time.

SELLING EXPENSES AND SELLING EXPENSES-TO-REVENUE RATIO
Selling expenses were 160.1 million baht, increased by 46.0 million baht, representing an increase of
40.3%, mainly due to higher operating expenses associated with branch expansion, including rental expenses,
utility expenses, salaries and employee benefits for branch staff, as well as marketing and promotional
expenses to support brand awareness and sales growth.
Selling expenses to revenue in Q1’26 were 28.6%, increased from 27.5% in Q1’25, mainly due to fixed costs
associated with newly opened branches during the initial stage of operations, resulting in lower fixed cost
absorption efficiency as such branches remained in the ramp-up period for revenue generation and operational
efficiency enhancement.

NET PROFIT AND NET PROFIT MARGIN (NPM)
Net profit was 34.2 million baht, increased by 1.7 million baht, representing an increase of 5.3%, mainly due to
revenue growth from sales and services following branch expansion and revenue recognition from newly opened
branches.
Net profit margin in Q1’26 was 6.1%, decreased from 7.8% in Q1’25, mainly due to lower gross profit margin and lower
fixed cost absorption efficiency in certain branches, driven by higher raw material costs and campaign mix in certain
brands, as well as higher rental expenses, depreciation expenses, and branch-related expenses associated with business
expansion. Nevertheless, administrative expenses to revenue improved following effective overhead cost control, which
partially offset the pressure on profitability, while the Company continued to focus on cost management and branch
efficiency enhancement to support long-term profitability.
